featured_reviews.name: Dhruvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was a student at Raj Computers (Malad – Nursing Lane). The teaching faculty is skilled and supportive, the syllabus is properly covered, and initially students were regularly informed about exam dates and circulars. Faculty also filled exam forms on behalf of students, which made the process smooth. The location is convenient, especially for students from Nagindas Khandwala College.

However, over time I faced repeated communication and coordination issues.

In 2023, I took a 4–6 month academic break due to my preponed 3-year LLB entrance exams. I informed the branch the same day and shared screenshots of my schedule. During admission, I was told breaks were allowed and full revision would be provided after course completion, which was one of the main reasons I enrolled. Later, in November 2024, the senior faculty in charge informed me that only doubts would be taken and not full revision, which was different from what I had understood earlier.

After my exams, I followed up in April–May 2024 to resume my DM course. Despite two in-person visits, including one in the senior faculty incharge’s presence, I was told no batch was available. In November 2024, I was informed that a WordPress batch had already started, but I had not been informed earlier and missed my first lecture.

In February 2025, I filled the exam form and paid the fees for the March exam, sharing the payment screenshot at the center itself. A week before the exam, I was told my form had not been processed because the screenshot had not been forwarded to the concerned teacher. As a result, I had to wait for the next exam cycle. My refund was processed only after I followed up.

Before my break, I regularly received exam circulars. However, in March and May 2025 I received no updates and learned about them only after asking. In July 2025, I again received no information and found out that internal exams were the next day only because I followed up in week three. A circular was later forwarded to me that others had already received. Despite paying exam fees on June 29 and asking about exam dates, I was not sent the circular. Exam update groups had existed for over a year, yet I was not added on either of my numbers until I raised the issue myself.

Through friends at other branches, I learned that similar communication issues had been experienced elsewhere, and some working students eventually stopped following up due to repeated visits.

In November 2025, while certificates were being distributed, I was informed that I had scored highest in the SMM exam and was asked to send my photograph to be framed and displayed. I shared my image, but I did not receive confirmation on how or where it was actually used, which left me uncertain.

Throughout my time as a student, I communicated clearly, paid fees on time, and followed up regularly, yet I often felt overlooked in batch scheduling, exam processing, and communication.

The teaching quality is commendable, but management and communication at the Nursing Lane branch need improvement. I am sharing this a few months after completing my courses because a friend had faced similar issues and eventually left without appearing for exams.

I hope the institute takes this feedback seriously and improves the experience for future students.
